name: M5Stack Unit ADC 0-12 V (ADS1100, I2C)
description: 16-bit I2C voltage meter for 0-12 V: the input terminal feeds a 300 kΩ / 100 kΩ divider (÷4), an LM358 voltage follower and a 1 kΩ resistor into a TI ADS1100 delta-sigma ADC (address 0x48, 8/16/32/128 SPS, PGA 1-8) whose reference is the unit's own 3.3 V rail (HT7533 regulator from the 5 V pin). The '-' terminal is ground. 4.7 kΩ SDA/SCL pull-ups go to the unit's 3.3 V, so the I2C lines stay at 3.3 V. Sold as: M5Stack Unit ADC (SKU U013), HY2.0-4P Grove socket (GND, 5V, SDA, SCL) plus a 2-pin HT3.96 screw terminal (+, -).
eli5: Measures a voltage between 0 and 12 V on its two screw terminals very precisely and sends the number to your board over two I2C wires.

pins.name: GND
pins.description: Ground (black wire of the Grove cable).

pins.name: 5V
pins.description: Supply, 5 V (red wire). Feeds the LM358 buffer directly and the HT7533 3.3 V regulator that powers the ADS1100 and the I2C pull-ups. With only 3.3 V here the LM358 output tops out near 1.8 V, so readings above about 7 V are lost.

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (yellow wire), 4.7 kΩ pull-up to the unit's 3.3 V rail.

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (white wire), 4.7 kΩ pull-up to the unit's 3.3 V rail.

pins.name: IN+
pins.description: '+' screw terminal: the voltage to measure, 0-12 V against '-'. Goes into a 300 kΩ / 100 kΩ divider (about 400 kΩ load).

pins.name: IN-
pins.description: '-' screw terminal: tied to the unit's GND (through a 0 Ω link) and to the ADS1100 VIN-. Not a floating differential input.

buildNotes: Two connectors: the HY2.0-4P Grove socket (black GND, red 5V, yellow SDA, white SCL) and a 2-pin HT3.96 screw terminal (+, -) for the measured voltage. Use a Grove-to-jumper cable for a breadboard.
Feed 5 V: the LM358 buffer runs from the 5V pin, and needs it to pass the full 3 V (12 V / 4) to the ADC. The I2C pull-ups go to the unit's own 3.3 V, so SDA/SCL are safe for an ESP32 or Pico.
The '-' terminal is the unit's GND: measure voltages referenced to your circuit's ground only, never across a component floating above ground.

Volts at the terminal = code x 3.3 V x 4 / 32768 at 8 SPS, PGA 1 (about 0.4 mV per code). The reference is the 3.3 V regulator output (±2 %), so calibrate against a multimeter for better than 2 % accuracy.
Single conversion: write one configuration byte 0x9C (ST/BSY=1, SC=1, 8 SPS, PGA 1), wait about 154 ms, read 3 bytes (code high, code low, config) and accept when bit 7 of the config byte is 0.
The I2C address is fixed at 0x48 (ADS1100A0). It clashes with ADS1115/ADS1015 boards at their default address.

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from m5_unit_adc import UnitADC

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}), freq=100000)
adc = UnitADC(i2c, addr=0x48, rate=8, gain=1)
while True:
    raw = adc.read_raw()
    print('ADC=%d %.3fV' % (raw, raw * adc.lsb()))
    time.sleep(1)

test.title: Reports the terminal voltage set on the slider
